extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, lawyers, and compliance officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance on §106.45(d) permissive dismissals, notification, appeals, and related procedural obligations for recipients' Title IX grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology discretion for grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion in how it communicates its obligations under §106.45(d) to students, including using different terminology than the final regulations (e.g., not necessarily using the word “dismissal”), provided it effectively conveys the circumstances in which a recipient may decline to initiate or continue a Title IX investigation or grievance procedures and otherwise complies with §106.45(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the same terminology as the final regulations can facilitate comparisons and enforcement, but recipients may choose terminology more appropriate to their student population (age, maturity, educational level). The key evaluative standard is whether the communication effectively conveys the circumstances for decline/continuation and complies with §106.45(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive (not mandatory) dismissal principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismissals under §106.45(d)(1) are permissive rather than mandatory: a recipient may dismiss a complaint if one of the listed grounds is satisfied, but is not required to do so and may instead initiate or continue grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may opt to investigate even when a permissive dismissal ground exists. The Department removed the 2020 mandatory dismissal requirement to avoid premature dismissal and to better fulfill Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate. Evaluators should check that recipients understand and apply permissive (discretionary) nature properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive list of permissive dismissal grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The four reasons listed in §106.45(d)(1) for permissive dismissal are exhaustive; unless one of those reasons applies, the recipient must implement grievance procedures under §106.45 (and, as applicable, §106.46) or an informal resolution under §106.44(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on additional, ad hoc grounds for dismissal (e.g., credibility assessments or uninvestigated factual determinations). If none of the four grounds applies, dismissal would be inconsistent with the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: recipient unable to identify the respondent (§106.45(d)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint if, after taking reasonable steps to identify the respondent, the respondent's identity cannot be ascertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps include interviewing the complainant, interviewing potential witnesses, and reviewing contemporaneous records (e.g., video footage, visitor logs). Even when the respondent is unknown, consider whether grievance procedures could proceed without a respondent to provide closure or address conditions (unsafe conditions, inadequate policies). Do not dismiss a policy/practice discrimination complaint simply because no individual respondent is named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: respondent not participating and not employed (§106.45(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint if the respondent is not participating in the recipient's education program or activity and is not employed by the recipient, but dismissal is discretionary, not mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Participating’ is broader than mere enrollment/disenrollment and can include alumni, volunteers, or attendance at recipient events. Recipients may nevertheless choose to implement grievance procedures if a non-student/non-employee's conduct otherwise falls within Title IX scope or poses ongoing risk. The regulation uses ‘and’ (both not participating AND not employed) to limit this dismissal option. If dismissal occurs, the recipient must still offer supportive measures and other steps to prevent recurrence; recipients may also bar third parties from events or reopen complaints if facts change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: complainant withdraws any or all allegations (§106.45(d)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss when the complainant voluntarily withdraws any or all allegations, but the recipient has discretion to determine if remaining allegations, if any, could independently constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal in this circumstance is fact-specific. The Title IX Coordinator must consider whether other factors (e.g., imminent safety threats) warrant initiating grievance procedures per §106.44(f)(1)(v). Dismissal for withdrawal does not relieve the recipient of obligations to address ongoing safety or access issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: alleged conduct would not constitute sex discrimination (§106.45(d)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may dismiss a complaint if the alleged conduct, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part, but must make reasonable efforts to clarify the allegations with the complainant before dismissing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying efforts protect complainants with limited English proficiency, disabilities, or misunderstandings of legal standards and help avoid mistaken dismissals. Recipients must not base dismissal on credibility or factual determinations without investigation. The Department declined to require mandatory dismissal in these cases to allow grievance procedures to gather information that could show the conduct meets Title IX standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify parties of dismissal and basis (§106.45(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify the complainant and, as applicable, the respondent of the dismissal and the basis for the dismissal; however, a respondent must only be notified of dismissal if the respondent previously had been notified of the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying a respondent who had no prior notice could cause confusion and safety risks for the complainant. The regulation contemplates simultaneous notice to parties when appropriate but does not mandate written notice in all contexts (especially K-12 situations). Documentation that the basis was communicated to the complainant (and respondent when applicable) is a best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights from dismissal (§106.45(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer an appeal from a dismissed complaint on the same bases required under the 2020 amendments: procedural irregularity; new evidence not reasonably available at the time of dismissal; or bias/conflict of interest of the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be available to both parties except when dismissal occurred before the respondent had been notified of the allegations (in which case respondent appeals may be conditioned). The Department cross-references these bases at §106.46(i)(1). Recipients are not required by the Department to provide written appeal decisions (particularly in elementary/secondary settings), though they may do so; recipients must ensure appeal decisionmakers are impartial and free of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to offer supportive measures and take prompt/effective steps after dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient that dismisses a complaint must offer supportive measures to the complainant and respondent, as appropriate, and take other prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur within the education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party, should protect safety and access to education, and are not punitive. Even when pursuing dismissal, recipients may have other legal obligations (e.g., Title VII) to investigate and address the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dismissal based on uninvestigated credibility or factual determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not dismiss complaints on grounds that depend on credibility assessments or factual determinations that require investigation; proper response to alleged retaliation or similar claims is to initiate an investigation under grievance procedures, not to dismiss the underlying complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents premature or biased dismissals. Evaluators should look for evidence that recipients are using pre-investigation credibility judgments as a basis for dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and training requirements for personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent, and must be trained on serving impartially (avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(2) and §106.8(d)(2)(iii). Evaluators should verify conflict-of-interest screening, training materials, and implementation (e.g., recusals, documentation). Bias concerns are also a stated basis for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to publish grievance procedures and provide access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must put its grievance procedures in writing under §106.45(a)(1) and include information on how to locate its grievance procedures in the notice of nondiscrimination disseminated to students under §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D). The Title IX Coordinator serves as a resource to explain procedures and answer questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should check that written procedures are accessible, that notice of nondiscrimination includes locating information, and that the Title IX Coordinator is identified and available as explained in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of ‘participating’ in education program or activity (terminology choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department chose the term ‘participating’ (rather than ‘accessing education benefits’) to be consistent with statutory and regulatory language; this impacts when §106.45(d)(1)(ii) dismissal may apply (requires respondent both not participating and not employed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should interpret ‘participating’ broadly to include activities like alumni roles, volunteers, or attendance at recipient events. Evaluators should ensure recipients are not inappropriately narrowing or expanding the meaning in ways inconsistent with Title IX terminology.
